ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian ذِمَّه دَار (zimma dār), from Arabic ذِمَّة (ḏimma, “protection, care, responsibility”) + Persian ـدار (-dār, “having”). Equivalent to ज़िम्मा (zimmā) + -दार (-dār). Cognate with Marathi जिम्मेदार (j̈immedār).

s.g: initialism of झारखंड मुक्ति मोर्चा (jhārkhaṇḍ mukti morcā)
to be put, placed, or laid; to be imposed

s.g: to put in possession (of), to occasion

ety.text: Hindi verb set बकना (baknā) बकवाना (bakvānā) Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *बक्कइ (bakkaï). Cognate with Maithili बकब (bakab) / 𑒥𑒏𑒥 (bakaba), Nepali बक्नु (baknu), Punjabi ਬਕਣਾ (bakṇā) / بَکݨا (bakṇā), Sindhi بَڪَڻُ (bakaṇu) / बकणु, Gujarati બકવું (bakvũ), Marathi बकणे (bakṇe), Odia ବକିବା (bakibā), Bengali বকা (boka), Assamese বকা (boka).
Orthographic borrowing from Bengali ময়মনসিংহ (moẏomnośiṅho), from a given name which would be equivalent to Hindi मोमिन (momin) + सिंह (sĩh).
Dissimilation from लोलना (lolnā), from Prakrit लोलइ (lolaï), from Sanskrit लोडयति (loḍayati, “to agitate”). False cognate of English roll. Related to आलोड़ना (āloṛnā, “to churn”), बिलोड़ना (biloṛnā).
Borrowed from Classical Persian وَزِیر (wazīr), from Arabic وَزِير (wazīr).

s.g: under consideration, pending, sub judice, under trial

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit विचाराधीन (vicārādhīna). By surface analysis, विचार (vicār) + अधीन (adhīn).
Learned borrowing from Sanskrit समष्टि (samaṣṭi). Cognate with Bengali সমস্ত (śomosto), Nepali समस्त (samasta) and Odia ସମସ୍ତ (samasta). Doublet of समष्टि (samaṣṭi).

s.g: a male given name, Himesh, from Sanskrit
